editorial:
Imagine you are a well-meaning teacher who just wants to do the right thing. That is exactly where you start with Carla. When some money goes missing at her school, she tries to solve the mystery without getting any kids in trouble. It sounds simple, but things quickly spiral out of control. You will feel the stress as Carla gets caught between her own morals and the strict rules of the school. The vibe is like a slow-burn thriller where a small mistake turns into a huge nightmare, making you wonder if you would have handled it any better.

What really hits home is the acting. You can see the panic on Carla's face as the parents and other teachers turn against her. The pacing is great because it keeps you on edge, even though it is just people talking in hallways. While some might find the lack of a big action climax a bit slow, the tension is real.
endingExplained: In the end, the truth comes out in a messy way. It turns out the actual thief was not who everyone thought. After a lot of fighting and accusations, the real culprit is revealed through a series of accidents and admissions. Carla does not get a big happy ending or a trophy for her honesty. Instead, she is left exhausted and broken, showing that trying to be the hero in a broken system often costs you everything.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves realistic dramas about human nature and conflict.
